studies.name: IPCC Special Report on Global Warming of 1.5°C (SR1.5)
studies.draft_uses: 2018 report — quantitative pathway timing figures: net zero CO2 'around 2050 (2045–2055 interquartile range)' for 1.5°C pathways; 'around 2070 (2065–2080 interquartile range)' for below-2°C pathways; CDR feasibility constraints; overshoot CDR role
studies.latest_known: SR1.5 (2018) was incorporated and updated by AR6 WGIII (April 2022) and AR6 SYR (March 2023). AR6 WGIII Chapter 3 updated net-zero CO2 timing for 1.5°C pathways to 'early 2050s' and for 2°C pathways to 'early 2070s' — broadly consistent but with revised scenario databases (SR1.5 used MAGICC6; AR6 used updated emulators). The draft cites both SR1.5 [3] and AR6 SYR [2] for net-zero timing, but the specific interquartile ranges (2045–2055; 2065–2080) are drawn from SR1.5's 2018 scenario set, which AR6 WGIII reassessed with a larger and updated scenario database.
studies.what_changed: The SR1.5 interquartile ranges for net-zero CO2 timing (2045–2055 for 1.5°C; 2065–2080 for below 2°C) were derived from the SR1.5 scenario set assessed with MAGICC6. AR6 WGIII (2022) reassessed these using an updated and larger scenario database with recalibrated emulators, reporting 'early 2050s' and 'early 2070s' as the central characterisation. The draft quotes the SR1.5 IQR figures as if they are the current best estimate, while the AR6 WGIII — which the draft also cites — is the more recent readout for these pathway statistics.

studies.name: Minx et al. 2018 — Negative emissions—Part 1: Research landscape and synthesis (Environmental Research Letters)
studies.draft_uses: 2018 paper — qualitative findings: BECCS dominance in large-scale removal scenarios; scepticism about 10–20 GtCO2/yr removals; moral hazard (negative emission technologies in cost-optimising models impede near-term reductions); soil carbon reversibility
studies.latest_known: The 2018 ERL paper has not been retracted or formally updated. The same lead authors (Minx, Lamb, Callaghan, Nemet, Smith, Geden) have produced the State of Carbon Dioxide Removal series (1st ed. January 2023; 2nd ed. June 2024; 3rd ed. June 2026, DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/ZRD65) as the successor assessment series. The 3rd edition (June 2026) reports current CDR at 2.2 GtCO2/yr, novel CDR still a tiny fraction, and a >5 GtCO2/yr gap between national pledges and 1.5°C-consistent levels by 2050.
studies.what_changed: The draft's qualitative claims drawn from Minx 2018 (BECCS dominance, scepticism about 10–20 GtCO2/yr, moral hazard) remain broadly consistent with the 2026 State of CDR findings. However, the 2018 paper's characterisation of the scenario landscape has been substantially updated: the 2nd and 3rd State of CDR editions identify a subset of 'more sustainable' 1.5°C scenarios requiring 7–9 GtCO2/yr by 2050 (not exclusively BECCS), and the 3rd edition (2026) provides new data on novel CDR growth rates (+36.1%/yr 2020–2025), voluntary markets, and MRV frameworks not available in 2018. The draft does not cite the State of CDR series at all, citing only the 2018 predecessor paper for the current state of the field.

studies.name: IEA Net Zero Emissions by 2050 Scenario — DACCS deployment figure
studies.draft_uses: Draft states: 'the IEA's Net Zero scenario deploys CDR on a limited scale, with DACCS removing 0.6 GtCO2 in 2050'
studies.latest_known: IEA 'Direct Air Capture: A key technology for net zero' (2024) states the IEA Net Zero Emissions by 2050 Scenario has DAC capturing approximately 980 MtCO2/year (~0.98 GtCO2/yr) by 2050. Multiple corroborating sources (IEA tracking page, IEAGHG 2025 report, independent analyses) confirm the ~980 Mt figure for the current NZE scenario.
studies.what_changed: The draft quotes 0.6 GtCO2 for DACCS in 2050 under the IEA NZE scenario. The current IEA NZE scenario figure is ~0.98 GtCO2/yr (980 MtCO2/yr) by 2050 — approximately 63% higher than the figure the draft uses. The 0.6 Gt figure appears to derive from an earlier version of the IEA NZE analysis or a different sub-category accounting; it does not match the figure in the current (2024) IEA DAC report.

studies.name: UK Net Zero Strategy (October 2021)
studies.draft_uses: Draft states: 'In the UK, the latest national plan, published in October 2021, proposes afforestation, wood in construction, soil carbon and BECCS, as well as DACCS, biochar and enhanced weathering'
studies.latest_known: The October 2021 Net Zero Strategy has been superseded twice: first by the March 2023 Carbon Budget Delivery Plan (itself ruled unlawful in May 2024), and then by the Carbon Budget and Growth Delivery Plan published 29 October 2025, which is now the UK government's current net-zero strategy document.
studies.what_changed: The draft describes the October 2021 document as 'the latest national plan', but the current UK net-zero strategy is the Carbon Budget and Growth Delivery Plan (October 2025). The 2025 plan significantly revises CDR ambitions: it reduces expected engineered greenhouse gas removals in 2030 to just 0.7 MtCO2 (down from 5.6 MtCO2 assumed in the 2023 plan), while maintaining a 2035 target of ~21.8 MtCO2. The 2021 document's specific CDR method list and scale assumptions are no longer the operative UK policy position.
